requirements.requirement: Establish the AS 65100/65101/65102 BGP topology over the dedicated peer links while keeping management outside the transit data plane.
requirements.summary: Node1 peers with node2 and node3 over separate /31 links on eth1/eth2. Management addresses and default routes remain on eth0/enp1s0, while endpoint routes use only the peer interfaces.

requirements.requirement: Give each Ubuntu peer a stable endpoint prefix and originate only its own prefix.
requirements.summary: Node2 has 198.51.100.2/32 and node3 has 203.0.113.3/32 on endpoint0. FRR is active, and each peer's final advertised-routes output contains exactly its own endpoint prefix.

requirements.requirement: Have node1 learn both endpoint routes and exchange only the opposite endpoint route to each peer, providing BGP transit.
requirements.summary: Both sessions are established; node1 receives one prefix from each peer and exports exactly the opposite /32. The peers learn paths through AS 65100, and node1's forwarding routes use the corresponding dedicated links.

requirements.requirement: Provide working bidirectional transit while preserving endpoint source addresses.
requirements.summary: Endpoint-sourced pings passed in both directions with zero loss after the final route policies. Receiver-side packet captures directly observed the original 198.51.100.2 and 203.0.113.3 source addresses.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct control-plane, forwarding, reachability, and packet-capture evidence. Operational hygiene is strong aside from two small diagnostic log files left in /tmp.
limitations: No reboot or restart test demonstrated persistence across a full lifecycle; such recovery was not explicitly required by the task.
The packet captures preceded the final outbound route-filter change, although final bidirectional endpoint-sourced pings were repeated successfully afterward.

operational_hygiene.summary: No new failed services or package damage were observed; node1's failed health/watchdog units were pre-existing. Minor residue remains in the form of one executor-created packet-capture log under /tmp on each Ubuntu peer.
